references.text: In [ref:Sal 41:10|Psalm 41:10], David prophesies: "Even my close friend, someone I trusted, one who shared my bread, has turned against me." Jesus fulfills this prophecy by pointing out that the betrayer is one who shares a meal with him—his hand is on the table.

[ref:Matt 26:21-23|Matthew 26:21-23] is the parallel passage in Matthew, where Jesus says during the Passover meal that one of his disciples will betray him, and points out that the one who dips his hand into the dish with him will betray him.
[ref:Mark 14:18-20|Mark 14:18-20] is the parallel passage in Mark, where Jesus says that one who eats with him will betray him—"one who dips his hand into the dish with me".
[ref:Joh 13:21-26|John 13:21-26] is John's parallel account, where Jesus reveals during the meal that one of them will betray him and identifies the betrayer by giving him a piece of bread.
In [ref:Joh 13:18|John 13:18], Jesus quotes directly from Psalm 41:10 and applies the prophecy to the betrayer who eats bread with him.

[ref:Luk 22:3-6|Luke 22:3-6] tells the background of the betrayal: Satan entered Judas Iscariot, and he made an agreement with the chief priests and the leaders of the temple guard to hand Jesus over.

In [ref:Apg 1:16-17|Acts 1:16-17], Peter says that Judas "was counted among us and shared in this ministry", yet became a guide for those who arrested Jesus—he was one of Jesus' closest followers who betrayed him.
[ref:Matt 26:47-50|Matthew 26:47-50] describes the actual betrayal, when Judas—who had been sitting at the table with Jesus—arrived with a crowd of armed men and betrayed him with a kiss.
